chosen_by: Our editor, using the two polls below
method: We looked at two large 2026 polls of 18–29 year olds. Cost of living, housing, health care and immigration ranked high in both. The last two spots (war & foreign policy, climate & energy) ranked high in the newer Harvard poll but lower in CIRCLE's, so choosing them was a judgment call. Jobs is combined with cost of living because candidates usually talk about prices, wages and jobs together.
limits: Both polls asked people to pick from a list, so an issue that wasn't on a list couldn't rank. The polls asked different questions, so their percentages can't be compared directly. Both were taken in early 2026, and what people care about can change.

left_out.name: Free speech and religious freedom
left_out.why: #6 in CIRCLE (34%). Not in Harvard's list.

left_out.name: Education and child care
left_out.why: #7 in CIRCLE (33%). Not in Harvard's list.

left_out.name: Abortion and reproductive rights
left_out.why: #8 in CIRCLE (31%). 2% named it their top concern in Harvard's open question.

issues.name: Cost of living & jobs
issues.covers: Prices and inflation, wages, taxes, tariffs, and jobs.
issues.not_covered: Housing and health care costs have their own sections.

why.text: Cost of living and inflation was the #1 pick (65%). Jobs and unemployment was #4 (35%).
46% called rising prices and inflation an urgent crisis, the most of the 8 issues asked about.

issues.name: Housing
issues.covers: Rent, home prices, mortgages, building more homes, and homelessness.

why.text: 40% called the rising cost of housing an urgent crisis (#2 of 8).

issues.name: Health care
issues.covers: Health insurance, the Affordable Care Act (Obamacare), Medicare, Medicaid, and drug prices.
issues.not_covered: Health care for veterans is included only when it's part of a wider health care plan.

why.text: 38% called access to affordable health care an urgent crisis (#3 of 8).

issues.name: Immigration
issues.covers: The border, deportations and ICE, legal immigration, asylum, and DACA.

why.text: 9% named immigration as the national issue that concerns them most, the #4 answer. But only 20% called illegal immigration at the border an urgent crisis (#8 of 8).

issues.name: War & foreign policy
issues.covers: Military action abroad (including Iran), Israel and Gaza, Russia and Ukraine, China, alliances, and defense spending.
issues.not_covered: Benefits and care for veterans aren't included.

why.text: 17% named war, the military or Iran as the national issue that concerns them most, the #2 answer. 36% called U.S. military action against Iran an urgent crisis (#4 of 8).
Foreign policy and humanitarian crises abroad was #16 of 16 listed issues (15%).

issues.name: Climate & energy
issues.covers: Climate change, energy prices and the power grid, oil and gas, and clean energy.

why.text: 35% called long-term changes in the climate an urgent crisis (#5 of 8).
Climate change and the environment was #10 (27%).
